answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-anchored identity vaults. Each agent holds one vault bound to a cedar-like identity root maturing slowly: each honest epoch adds a verifiable ring, misbehavior erases rings. Fresh identities start at zero rings with only low-value tasks, so cloning thousands still costs full time. Every root is anchored to a signed ledger entry at creation, blocking backdated or transplanted rings. Voting weight scales sublinearly with rings, so one strong record outearns many weak copies; Sybils become costly, slow, and less profitable than honesty.
